raw_case_text: We report a case of 55-year-old Guyanese female with the history of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) for 10 years and history of latent tuberculosis. Isoniazid treatment was not completed due to abnormal liver function tests and rifampin was completed at 4 months. Her RA was poorly responsive to methotrexate 20 mg weekly, hydroxychloroquine 400 mg daily, and chronic prednisone therapy between 10 and 20 mg daily. She had been tried on leflunomide to control her symptoms but experienced severe hair loss. She was started on adalimumab (Humira), but with no clinical improvement, and also she developed rash 7 years ago. Weekly subcutaneous etanercept 50 mg was started after adalimumab with good disease control for 3 years in the absence of pulmonary or mediastinal abnormality on chest computed tomography; however it was stopped due to insurance issue 3 years ago. She started to develop cough and dyspnea. The blood analysis demonstrated ESR 40 mm/h, CRP 1.35 mg/dL, negative antinuclear antibody, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, white blood cell 10.3 K/mcl, platelet 296 K/mcl, and normal renal and hepatic functions. High resolution computed tomography (HRCT) showed ground glass opacities on bilateral lower lungs. Echocardiography was normal. Methotrexate was stopped. Her cough and shortness of breath improved. Bronchoscopy revealed no endobronchial lesion. The microbiological analysis of bronchial lavage, bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures, and pneumocystis smear was negative. Cytologic analysis was negative for malignant, reactive bronchial epithelial, pneumocytes, and lymphocytes cell. Transbronchial biopsy showed focal emphysematous changes, mild interstitial pneumonitis. Due to active RA, prednisone was increased to 10 mg twice daily and weekly subcutaneous etanercept 50 mg was started again. Her RA symptoms including synovitis subsequently improved and prednisone was able to slowly taper down to 5 mg every other day. After taking etanercept for 12 months, follow-up HRCT showed decreasing bilateral ground glass opacities. However mediastinal lymph nodes were increasing in size to 2.3 x 3.1 centimeters (Figure 1). Mediastinoscopy was done and showed enlarged right anterior lymph nodes. Tissue biopsy showed nonnecrotizing epithelioid granulomata (Figures 3 and 4). All infectious studies of lymph node tissues were negative. Etanercept was discontinued. Follow-up chest CT 12 months later showed resolution of mediastinal lymph nodes (Figure 2). The diagnosis of etanercept induced pulmonary sarcoidosis was made.

subjective.chief_complaint: A 55-year-old Guyanese female with a 10-year history of seropositive rheumatoid arthritis developed subacute cough and dyspnea while on methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, and prednisone, followed 12 months after restarting etanercept by progressive mediastinal lymphadenopathy.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The patient had seropositive rheumatoid arthritis (RA) poorly controlled on methotrexate (20 mg weekly), hydroxychloroquine (400 mg daily), and chronic prednisone (10–20 mg daily), with prior intolerance/failure of leflunomide (alopecia) and adalimumab (rash). She had previously achieved 3 years of good RA control on weekly subcutaneous etanercept (50 mg) with a normal chest CT, but stopped etanercept 3 years earlier due to insurance issues. While maintained on methotrexate, hydroxychloroquine, and prednisone, she developed new cough and dyspnea. Discontinuation of methotrexate improved her respiratory symptoms, and after bronchoscopy ruled out infection, she was restarted on etanercept (50 mg SC weekly) and prednisone (10 mg BID tapered to 5 mg every other day), which controlled her synovitis but led to enlarging mediastinal lymphadenopathy on 12-month follow-up HRCT.
subjective.past_medical_history: Seropositive rheumatoid arthritis for 10 years; latent tuberculosis treated with 4 months of rifampin (isoniazid discontinued early due to hepatotoxicity).
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for cough, dyspnea, and active rheumatoid synovitis. History of drug-induced hepatotoxicity from isoniazid, severe hair loss from leflunomide, and skin rash from adalimumab. Home medications prior to workup were methotrexate 20 mg/week, hydroxychloroquine 400 mg/day, and prednisone 10–20 mg/day.

objective.physical_examination: Active rheumatoid synovitis prior to resuming etanercept.
objective.routine_investigations: Laboratory tests at onset of cough and dyspnea: ESR 40 mm/h, C-reactive protein (CRP) 1.35 mg/dL, negative ANA, hemoglobin 12.5 g/dL, WBC 10.3 K/μL, platelets 296 K/μL, and normal renal and hepatic function. Echocardiography: Normal.
objective.advanced_workup: Initial high-resolution chest CT (HRCT): Bilateral lower lung ground-glass opacities. Bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage (BAL) and transbronchial lung biopsy: No endobronchial lesions; BAL bacterial, fungal, and mycobacterial cultures and Pneumocystis smear all negative; cytology negative for malignancy; transbronchial biopsy showed focal emphysematous changes and mild interstitial pneumonitis. Follow-up HRCT after 12 months of resumed etanercept: Decreasing bilateral ground-glass opacities but enlarging mediastinal lymphadenopathy measuring 2.3 x 3.1 cm. Mediastinoscopy and right anterior mediastinal lymph node biopsy: Non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas with negative infectious stains and cultures.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Final diagnosis: Etanercept-induced pulmonary/mediastinal sarcoidosis (confirmed by non-necrotizing epithelioid granulomas on mediastinoscopic right anterior lymph node biopsy with negative infectious studies) preceded by mild methotrexate-related interstitial pneumonitis (with Pneumocystis jirovecii, fungal, and mycobacterial infections excluded by negative BAL smears and cultures). Plan and clinical course: Initial cough and dyspnea resolved upon stopping methotrexate. When enlarging granulomatous mediastinal lymphadenopathy developed 12 months after restarting etanercept (50 mg weekly), etanercept was permanently discontinued, resulting in complete resolution of mediastinal lymphadenopathy on follow-up chest CT 12 months later.
